The claim holds, with some caveats below. I did not dispatch any workflow and wrote nothing in any repository. Notes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/rc-smoke.md.

1. The code at 048bc84 (tools/screening-capacity/limits.ts:289-412):
- requiredCpus(limits) = sharedLayoutCpus = Postgres 2 + consumer 2 = 4 CPUs.
- runnerTooSmall fails only if the runner has fewer than 4 CPUs, or if Postgres would get less than MIN_POSTGRES_MIB. That memory is the smaller of 4 GiB and the runner's memory minus the tasks and a reserve, so a 16 GiB runner passes.
- 8 CPUs only switches cpuLayout to the "own" layout (each service on its own CPUs). Nothing requires it. On 4 CPUs the harness reports the shared layout (expected.layout.kind).
- release-capacity.yml runs on ubuntu-26.04 and runs the harness under taskset at --print-harness-cpus (0-1). It has a workflow_dispatch trigger with no branch guard.
- `gh api repos/PureTideWater/PhysicalTherapy` says visibility public, so ubuntu-26.04 is GitHub's free 4-CPU runner.

2. The two runs (I read them with `gh api .../actions/runs/<id>` and `.../actions/jobs/<job>/logs`, read-only):
- 40479127979: scheduled, claude/build-platform at e908c21, capacity job 122104699853 on ubuntu-24.04.
  - Runner line: "harness on CPUs 0-1", then "runner 4 CPUs, 15989 MiB; runtime docker; worker 0.5 vCPU and 1024 MiB on CPUs 3".
  - It seeded A at 100,000 lines with release 900110 (4,172,393 records), so this was full size.
  - Verdict: "verdict: fail". A's triage and A's audit report failed, with JOB_FAILED 2 times. This is the "fails first" failure CAS-42.5 expects.
- 40584379787: workflow_dispatch on the branch co-001/ci-browser at 6484324, job 122471867560 on ubuntu-26.04.
  - Runner line: "runner 4 CPUs, 15983 MiB; runtime docker".
  - Verdict: "verdict: fail", for the same reason.
- Neither run hit RUNNER_TOO_SMALL. Both reached a verdict on 4 CPUs.

3. The local smoke run (process runtime, this container: 4 CPUs, 16 GiB, cgroup v1, root):
- Commands:
  - `git -C /home/user/PhysicalTherapy worktree add --detach .../scratchpad/rc 048bc84`
  - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: exit 0

- Chromium: the process runtime passes the worker only PATH and HOME, so I set HOME to a scratch directory whose .cache/ms-playwright links to /opt/pw-browsers.

Run command: `HOME=<scratch home> flock /tmp/laneb-heavy.lock taskset -c 0-1 pnpm exec tsx tools/release-capacity/run.ts --out <scratch out> --runtime process --images <rc-img> --admin-url postgres://postgres:test@localhost:5433/postgres --database tp_rcsmoke_1 --small`
- Result: exit 0 in about 72 s.
  - Runner line: "runner 4 CPUs, 16091 MiB; runtime process", so it passed the RUNNER_TOO_SMALL check.
  - Verdict: "verdict: pass" at smoke size. All 19 jobs completed on attempt 1, across every phase: setup, concurrent, chain, A's reconcile and the large jobs together.
  - Priced lines 2000 of 2000; parsed claims 400 of 400; memory peak 421.9 of 1024 MiB; at most 1 advisory lock per backend.
  - Two QUEUE_ERROR lines came after the verdict, during teardown, when the database is dropped.
- Saved copies: .../scratchpad/logs/rc-smoke.log, rc-smoke-summary.md and rc-smoke-release-capacity.json.
- Cleanup: the scratch worktree and its rc-img, home and out directories are removed. The harness dropped tp_rcsmoke_1 itself; a later DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS confirmed it was gone.

Caveats:
- A dispatch whose capacity job fails also runs the notify job (it is skipped only for pull_request events), which opens or comments on the issue "Release capacity test failing", naming the branch. CAS-42.5's head run is expected to pass. Any failure, or an advisory such as the windows query running over its budget (run 40479127979 logged 51 s cold against 5 s), will write to that issue.
- A process-runtime run records Commit `unknown`, because run.ts runs `git rev-parse` inside the images' worker directory and the copy is not a git checkout. The before and after summaries must name their commits by hand in the PR.
- The process runtime uses the caller's unlimited Postgres. It never restarts it, so cache is not dropped and no netem delay is applied (these are reported as departures from production). So the local CAS-42.6 compares base against head; it is not a production-class measurement. The design's own wording for .6 says `--worker-image`, but Docker has no daemon here, so the process route is the only local one, as section 8.2 provides.
- The claim needs a public repository. If the repository goes private, ubuntu-26.04 has 2 CPUs and run.ts refuses with RUNNER_TOO_SMALL, as the workflow comment says.
- Neither run needs the founder. Only the domain-model approval and Q1 go to the founder (section 10).

CAS-42.5 (at PR time, run by Lane A; this agent dispatched nothing). Read-only checks first, then the dispatch:
  gh api repos/PureTideWater/PhysicalTherapy --jq .visibility   # must print public
  gh workflow run release-capacity.yml --repo PureTideWater/PhysicalTherapy --ref co-001/suite-cap-1-triage-locks
  gh run list --repo PureTideWater/PhysicalTherapy --workflow release-capacity.yml --branch co-001/suite-cap-1-triage-locks --limit 1 --json databaseId,headSha
  gh run watch <id> --repo PureTideWater/PhysicalTherapy --exit-status; gh run download <id> --repo PureTideWater/PhysicalTherapy -n release-capacity -D <dir>
  # Check: the job log shows "runner 4 CPUs", headSha equals the PR head, and summary.md is pasted into the PR. A failure or advisory also comments on the "Release capacity test failing" issue.

CAS-42.6 (local, process runtime; base = SUITE-CAP-1a's merge, head = PR head; one shared release dir; heavy steps one at a time under the lock):
  export PATH=/opt/node24/bin:/opt/pnpm-bin:/opt/py312-ci/bin:$PATH; R=<scratch>
  for side in base head; do
    git -C /home/user/PhysicalTherapy worktree add --detach $R/$side <base-sha|head-sha>
    (cd $R/$side && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && flock /tmp/laneb-heavy.lock pnpm --filter @tp/worker build)
    mkdir -p $R/img-$side/worker/node_modules $R/img-$side/web
    cp -R $R/$side/apps/worker/dist $R/img-$side/worker/dist
    cp -R $R/$side/packages/db/migrations $R/img-$side/worker/migrations
    cp -RL $R/$side/apps/worker/node_modules/playwright-core $R/img-$side/worker/node_modules/
  done
  mkdir -p $R/home/.cache && ln -sfn /opt/pw-browsers $R/home/.cache/ms-playwright
  (cd $R/head && NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144 flock /tmp/laneb-heavy.lock pnpm exec tsx tools/release/scale.ts --shape quarterly --out $R/quarterly-release)
  cd $R/head; cpus=$(pnpm -s exec tsx tools/release-capacity/run.ts --print-harness-cpus)
  for side in base head; do
    HOME=$R/home flock /tmp/laneb-heavy.lock taskset -c "$cpus" pnpm exec tsx tools/release-capacity/run.ts --out $R/out-$side --runtime process --images $R/img-$side --admin-url postgres://postgres:test@localhost:5433/postgres --database tp_capacity_$side --release-dir $R/quarterly-release
  done
  # Run in the background (60 to 120 min each). Put $R/out-base/summary.md and $R/out-head/summary.md in the PR, naming each side's commit by hand (both summaries record Commit unknown).
  # The harness runs from the head checkout for both sides; only --images changes.
  # Cleanup: git worktree remove for both sides, rm -rf $R, and DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS tp_capacity_base and tp_capacity_head.

results.head: 74a6b29081101d7c9e3544e86ea15ba49ecaa6c8
fixes: Seam read found one defect, now fixed in commit 74a6b290 and pushed (d37a0ee3..74a6b290 on the first try, with the pre-push hook). The problem: a take-back was capped only at what the chain held on a line (interestHeld, which floors at zero), not at the line's interest as a whole. When two chains hold interest on one line and a contract specialist has lowered one chain's paid entry after its take-back, the other chain's take-back pushes the line below zero. Postgres's ledger_interest_line_floor then refuses it, which rolls back the practice's whole reconcile on every run. That breaks D8 ('the worker checks each bound before it writes; a valid reconcile is never refused').

The fix is in apps/worker/src/reconcile/remittances.ts recordInterest. A new lineHeld map holds each line's whole interest net of corrections and take-backs, computed with interestHeld over every interest match. Each take-back line's heldCents is now min(what the chain holds, lineHeld). No change to interest.ts, the migration, any amount, stage or recovered.

The test was written to fail first: a new case in apps/worker/src/reconcile/interest.db.test.ts, 'takes back from a line no more than its interest as a whole, when two chains hold interest there and a specialist lowered one (D5, D8)'. Before the fix it failed with Postgres's refusal 'a line's interest, net of what the payer took back, never goes below zero' (logs/fin-int-integ-floor-base.log). After the fix, interest, chain and ledger-oracle db tests: 3 files, 46/46 passed (logs/fin-int-integ-floor-head.log).
The domain model was regenerated on a freshly migrated database. Only its provenance line changed, and it is committed in 74a6b290.
